items.text: The Guide now explains MIDI: mapping a knob, mapping pads, Pads in order, and MIDI out with clock, and says plainly which browsers have it.

Statistics now says where the sound sits, left to right: in the score (each sounding mark at the place Grid space gives it) and in what has been heard so far, with the sound's lean, its spread, a histogram of both, a strip per colour, and how much of the score a Stereo binaural beat would reach. And the numbers can be taken away for other tools: a JSON report with everything, a CSV of the marks (place, colour, shape, pan, depth) and a CSV of every note heard (time, colour, shape, note, velocity, pan, depth). Grid space must be on for the sound to leave the middle.

Binaural beat: recordings and captures now include it (they took the unshifted mix before). And a third source, "Your piece, stereo": it keeps the stereo picture and shifts only the right channel, so sounds heard in both ears beat, sounds panned toward one side beat less, and a sound hard to one side not at all. "Your piece, mono" (before: "Your piece") still makes everything beat, at the price of the stereo picture. The Guide in the Index now explains the three sources and why mono and stereo trade off.

The binaural beat can now use your piece, not just two tones. In the Sounds display, hold the headphones button and choose "Your piece": the whole composition plays in both ears and the right ear is shifted up by the beat's few Hz (Delta 2, Theta 6, Alpha 10, or Tempo), so everything you hear beats against itself. It is a frequency shift, not a pitch shift: every partial moves by the same Hz, so the right ear is slightly detuned, and the piece is summed to mono while it is on. Headphones needed. Recordings and captures still take the unshifted mix. "Two tones" is still the default.

a binaural beat, one headphones button on the right rail. It adds two pure tones, one in each ear, tuned to your root note and a few Hz apart, which you hear as a slow pulse. Tap to switch it on; hold for its settings in the Sounds display: Delta (2 Hz), Theta (6 Hz), Alpha (10 Hz), or Tempo, where the beat is the grid's own pulse (tempo divided by 60). Soft, Medium or Clear level. It needs headphones, starts off every time, and is a sound layer, not a treatment.

The Hold hand has its own animation, like the waves off the finger's tip: while Hold is on, the line across the fist vibrates and short dashes radiate out from it to the left and right. Reduced-motion settings get still dashes.

iPhone upright: the grid now sizes itself to what is left of the screen, in play and in edit, so the whole thing (grid, colour and shape strip, bottom bar) fits on one screen. In edit the grid shrinks to make room for the strip.

iPhone upright: the empty gap between the grid and the bottom bar is gone. The bar sits right under the grid again and fits on the screen. In edit, the colour and shape strip now takes its room from the grid instead of pushing the bar down.
